claim: Across about 41M papers, higher reference atypicality goes with LOWER disruption (D) in every discipline, period and team-size stratum; effect size only in figures. (Gap search: full text has no coefficient, window or code; size unrecoverable.)
agent_test: Tag each candidate attempt as distant-mix or replace-the-leader; check whether distant-mix attempts replace the leading answer less often at equal tokens.

claim: The sign of the A-D link is contested: Lin, Evans, Wu 2022 report typicality vs D r=-0.05 (atypical = more disruptive; novel 61% vs 36% disruptive) while Li, Lin, Wu 2025 report atypical = less disruptive. Same group, different atypicality construction and sign convention. Gap search: no re-run on one corpus exists; candidate causes are MAG vs OpenAlex, median z vs top-tail A-index, longest D window to 2018 vs unstated window.
agent_test: Do not build a rule on the sign. Measure on our own agent whether distant-analogy attempts or in-topic rival attempts displace the incumbent answer more.

claim: Disruption (D) is best read as displacement of a dominant idea within its topic: disruptive papers share a field with their top reference far more than expected (0.52 vs a model-predicted 0.014), and a 20-scholar survey gives AUC 0.83.
agent_test: Add an explicit displacement attempt that targets the current best hypothesis in its own frame, separate from analogy attempts.

claim: The D index is biased by data artefacts: missing references create CD5=1 records (97% of CD5=1 papers, 78% of patents have zero references in the database); adding a zero-reference dummy lifts R2 from 0.15 to 0.95 (papers).
agent_test: None for the agent; use as warning that a single scalar novelty metric can be an artefact of input length or missing fields.

claim: D depends on reference-list length and network growth: citations grow ~5.1%/yr (double every 13.6 yr); in PNAS vs PNAS Plus the whole gap tracks reference count (b_r=-0.0039); ~35% CD drop from 20 years of density.
agent_test: Control for output/context length when scoring novelty or disruption of agent attempts.

claim: The reported decline in disruption (Park et al. 2023) is largely or partly an artefact of citation growth, reference lengthening and data errors; the same-team defenders show windowing choices change the picture.
agent_test: When comparing agent variants, fix window and length; do not read a falling novelty score as falling quality.

claim: D validity is mixed: convergent validity evidence 'not entirely conclusive', DI5 better than DI1; Nobel papers do not always score higher (Wei 2020 mean D 0.236 vs 0.239, p=0.898); Science Breakthrough of the Year AUC below 0.5; country counts (Iraq 57.5% D>0) look wrong.
agent_test: Never use D-like citation scores as reward; use outcome checks.

claim: Specification uncertainty is large: many-analyst studies find broad ranges of results on the same data and question, and D variants disagree.
agent_test: Report novelty results across several metric variants, not one.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: A modified measure (1D, pairwise) classifies benchmark prizes much better than D (AUC 0.94-0.98 vs 0.26-0.79, Nobel 0.73 for D); the same pairwise approach reverses the large-team conclusion. Gap search: the Nobel 1D AUC 0.981 is in the supplement table (D 0.731); second group (Huang/Xie) is on papers only, patents untested.
agent_test: Prefer pairwise comparison to the single most relevant incumbent over aggregate scores.

claim: Generalization (new idea that subsumes many prior ones) is the mechanism behind most disruptive citations (73.96%), D correlates r=0.37 with generalization and -0.37 with extension; semantic atypicality predicts awards in all domains, while reference atypicality is weak. Award odds: one SD of F index raises Nobel odds by about 58% to 104%; no award test on independent data found.
agent_test: Add a test: attempts that unify two prior solutions into a more general rule vs attempts that extend one solution.

claim: Methods and theory differ: new methods raise D, new theories and results lower it; LLM classification of 50,147 disruptive papers shows theory displacement is slower than method displacement.
agent_test: Treat method change and rule change as separate attempt types.

claim: LLM-generated research ideas are rated more novel than expert ideas in blind review (4.84 human vs 5.64 AI vs 5.81 AI+rerank; N=49 per condition, 79 reviewers; feasibility not different).
agent_test: Compare agent ideas to a human or baseline pool on blind ratings.

claim: LLM-idea novelty does not survive execution: after experts executed ideas (N=43), AI ideas lost 1.05 novelty, 1.76 excitement, 1.88 effectiveness points vs near 0 for human ideas.
agent_test: Verify novelty claims by running the idea (execution check) before accepting; novelty is not the reward.

claim: LLM ideas lack diversity and are often borrowed: only ~5% of 4000 seed ideas are non-duplicates; 24% of 50 LLM documents were paraphrased or heavily borrowed; 79.3% of ideas are dominated by 1-2 retrieved papers. Retrieval cuts within-set diversity 5.6-17.9% and raises pooled diversity 10.2-18.1% (45,000 ideas).
agent_test: Add dedup check across attempts at equal tokens; measure distinct-idea count.

claim: LLM-as-judge of novelty/quality is weak: best 53.3% pairwise (chance 50%), 71.4% accepted-vs-rejected; LLM rater AUC 0.42 for highly cited ICLR papers; reviewer score vs disruptiveness |rho|<=0.005.
agent_test: Do not use the same LLM as sole judge of novelty; use external checks.

claim: Search strategy for ideation matters: iterative planning and search gives 3.4x more unique ideas (Nova); autonomous agent runs (3,222) rated none Original and had fabrications.
agent_test: Test planned retrieval-driven search vs plain sampling at equal tokens, counting unique non-duplicate, checked ideas.

claim: Open-source model-network disruption: most models are consolidating (mean MDI -0.53); larger models are somewhat less consolidating.
agent_test: None direct.

claim: Uzzi 2013: papers with a conventional core plus a novel tail are hits (top 5% citations) 9.11 per 100 vs background 5; conventional-only 5.82, novel-only 5.33, neither 2.05; teams 37.7% more likely to add novel combinations.
agent_test: Compare attempts that add one distant element to a standard method against fully distant and fully standard attempts, at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: In executed ML-research agent search (3,222 runs, six strategies) no idea was rated Original and only one idea was both top-10 in quality and weakly novel; polishing the known recipe won on quality in 2 of 3 domains.
agent_test: Use execution result as the first rank; add novelty only as a tie-break; audit the verifier for fabrication (2.5% of runs).

claim: A learned prefilter plus execution in math/code search (AlphaResearch) filtered 151 ideas, correctly rejecting 108 failures and wrongly rejecting 43 viable ones; 2 of 8 open problems beaten.
agent_test: Measure false-reject rate of any cheap filter before use.

claim: Text-embedding (semantic) atypicality predicts major awards across domains better than reference-list atypicality or D, but only on one group's data.
agent_test: Use embedding distance between attempt and incumbent as a cheap atypicality score; check against execution wins.
